key_insight: Recursive, weight-sharing transformer designs can outperform over-parameterized surrogates on small engineering datasets by trading extra compute for far fewer learnable parameters.
engineering_relevance: This matters for semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability workflows where repeated finite-element analyses of stress and warpage are expensive, so compact surrogate models can accelerate design-space exploration.
method: Compared three recursive transformer variants: Tiny Recursive Model, Depth Recursive Transformer, and a simple recursive transformer.
Evaluated surrogate accuracy and efficiency using Recall, Mean Reciprocal Rank, parameter count, and FLOPs.
Validated the approach on two low-dimensional tasks: semiconductor package thermo-mechanical reliability and a Laplace PDE capacitance-field solver.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic hardware-aware evaluation on small, low-dimensional engineering datasets, showing that recursive weight-sharing models balance predictive performance with lower parameter and memory cost.
watch_item: Because the datasets are low-dimensional and simulation data is limited, the reported gains may not transfer directly to large, highly nonlinear design spaces without re-tuning.
paper_title: Recursive transformers for semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability
